crop.notes: Whole 'Answers to Correspondents' column, headline to end. Only the 'Subscriber' answer near the bottom (Allen and McCoole saloon locations) is about Allen; the rest are unrelated reader questions.

ocr.notes: Readable; a few garbled names (Bessehi, McCoodle) but the Allen item is accurate.

title.suggested: Where Tom Allen and Mike McCoole kept saloons

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch told a reader that at the first Allen-McCoole fight Allen kept a saloon on Broadway between O'Fallon and Biddle, and that before the second fight he moved it to Washington Avenue between Fourth and Broadway.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Sunday, February 17, 1889, page 4.

facts.fact: At the time of his first fight with Mike McCoole, Allen kept a saloon on Broadway between O'Fallon and Biddle streets, St. Louis
places: Broadway between O'Fallon and Biddle streets, St. Louis

facts.fact: Before his second fight with McCoole, Allen moved his saloon to Washington Avenue between Fourth Street and Broadway, St. Louis
places: Washington Avenue between Fourth Street and Broadway, St. Louis

facts.fact: McCoole kept a saloon on Broadway between Market and Chestnut at the first fight, later moving to the corner of Broadway and Wash Street
places: Broadway between Market and Chestnut streets, St. Louis
Broadway and Wash Street, St. Louis

notes: A one-paragraph reader answer written 1889, so the saloon dates are retrospective (first fight 1869, second fight 1873). The Allen item is entirely about his and McCoole's saloons, hence primary.
